title: The Old Church Bell
summary: In the small town of Marbach in Germany, an old church bell hung in the church tower. When a great storm cracked its bronze rim, the town melted the metal into a smaller bell....
full_text:
In the small town of Marbach in Germany, an old church bell hung in the church tower. When a great storm cracked its bronze rim, the town melted the metal into a smaller bell.

On the night the bell was recast, a poor army surgeon's wife gave birth to a frail infant boy in a humble garret. The church bell tolled, and its chime seemed to weave a prophecy around the child's cradle: "Thou shalt ring out a song of freedom that will shake the thrones of tyrants!"

That child was Friedrich Schiller—the glorious poet who wrote the Ode to Joy and the Song of the Bell! His fiery verse swept across Europe like a thunderstorm, inspiring millions to stand for human liberty, dignity, and brotherhood.

The old bronze bell had cracked, but the poetry born under its chime rings on through centuries, an unbreakable anthem of the free human spirit.
moral: The bell of true freedom and poetry rings from humble cradles to awaken the conscience of nations.
